title: Recursion Introduction
learningObjectives: Explain recursion as a function calling itself.
Identify base cases and the step that reduces the problem.
Trace nested calls and unwind returned values.
Implement recursive logic and compare with an iterative alternative.

understand.concept: A recursive function calls itself to solve a smaller or simpler instance. Recursion needs a base case and progress toward it. Each active call uses call-stack space.
understand.whyItMatters: Recursion can express problems such as tree traversal and divide-and-conquer, though an iterative solution may be safer for very deep repetitions.
understand.explain: Trace calls downward until the base case, then trace returns upward. Ensure the recursive argument changes toward termination. Test small inputs and be cautious about stack depth and repeated work.

examples.explanation: The base case stops recursion; use for nonnegative n and beware large-value overflow.

examples.title: Countdown trace

examples.title: Naive Fibonacci
examples.explanation: This simple recursion repeats calculations and grows exponentially.

examples.title: Recursive array sum
examples.code: int sum(const int* a,int n){if(n==0)return 0;return a[n-1]+sum(a,n-1);}
examples.explanation: The count decreases; the caller must supply a valid pointer and length.

practise.guidedTask: For Recursion Introduction, analyze each example and record the parameter signature, call, chosen behavior, state changes and result. Identify any compile-time constraints or design caveats.
practise.independentTask: Create a focused C++ exercise on Recursion Introduction. Include several cases demonstrating the main concept, plus tests for typical, boundary and invalid/ambiguous cases as appropriate. State the expected behavior and verify each case.
hints: Identify the concept being demonstrated before tracing code.
Use small, explicit examples to verify behavior.
Compare at least two contrasting cases.
Check compiler rules, lifetime and error paths relevant to this topic.
Keep the code focused and explain the observed output/result.
